correctness.rationale: For every n>=4 and 2<=k<n, the exact shortcut link is Delta(e_1,...,e_{k-2}) * boundary(Delta(e_k,...,e_{n-1})). This follows from the two local arc conflicts and the unique residual cycle s,e_k,...,e_{n-1}. For k>=3, toggling e_1 for s-containing faces gives a decreasing-dimension free-face collapse onto the original cycle boundary. For k=2 the link is S^{n-4}, embedded nullhomotopically in S^{n-2}, so the cone attachment yields S^{n-2} wedge S^{n-3}. All integer parameter boundaries are addressed. The included verifier independently checks exact faces, Betti vectors and 1291 elementary collapse pairs for 35 cases, as supplemental finite evidence.

value.rationale: The explicit new cyclic-digraph problem in arXiv:2602.14936 motivates the first natural edge-addition test. For the entire two-parameter family, the integral homotopy type changes only at the sharp shortcut length two. An explicit relative simplicial collapse distinguishes the stable cases at a substantially stronger level than Betti numbers, while the exceptional case creates a new lower-dimensional infinite-cyclic class. This all-size boundary phenomenon is mathematically explanatory, not a fabricated parameter slice or a restatement of the unchorded result.
